brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Bases at level 0 (piece:0,0,0;half-n, piece:-1,0,0;full) and level 1 (piece:0,0,1;half-n, piece:-1,0,1;full) with snaps locking levels; check_build meshClash clear.
Two drawers placed: drawer:0#0,0#cut (level 0 south cut face) and drawer:1#0,0#cut (level 1 south cut face) from half-n bases.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for workbench use (stable tower form)
requirements.evidence: Two-storey column provides stacked storage footprint; LOOSE_BODY warning remains (piece:0,0,0;half-n not joint-bolted) and open faces uncapped - functional but not yet locked/capped per house rules as final dressing was skipped per user stop instruction.

finish.summary: Built two-storey tower with two half-n stacked at 0,0 providing two south-facing drawers, plus adjacent full column at -1,0 for two-storey height and stability. Mesh is clear. Check shows LOOSE_BODY and open caps pending final lock/cap, acceptable per stop instruction.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
